historical_growth.window_note: FY2019-FY2025 only (merged-entity history). FY2026 is excluded as a partial-year acquisition step-up.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: segment-weighted organic growth of the post-acquisition entity (see base narrative); equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (1.4%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (7.4%) and EPS (10.5%): book equity is dominated by 2018 merger goodwill and nearly all earnings are paid out or were bought back, so it carries no growth signal. Not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes; no interest-income strip, the company is a net debtor): FY2020 1,910, FY2022 2,417, FY2025 1,377. Owner FCF fell while revenue and EPS rose: FY2023-FY2025 cash conversion was depressed by working-capital investment, distribution-rights and GHOST-related payments and higher capex. SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are within ~2pp of each other, so SBC is not what is eating the cash flow; SBC is ~0.6-0.8% of revenue. FY2025-to-FY2026 comparisons are meaningless on a reported basis (JDE Peet's from Q2-2026).

scenario_narratives.base: Segment-weighted ~3% growth: U.S. Refreshment Beverages (~40% of pro forma sales) slows from ~10% to mid-single digits as GHOST and the energy/hydration distribution deals lap; legacy U.S. Coffee (~14%) is flat to slightly down, with K-Cup pod volume still shrinking (-4.8% FY2025, -6.8%/-12.8%/-0.5% across Q1-Q3 2026) and pricing now giving back (-4.2% in Q3-2026); KDP International (~9%) grows mid-single digits on Mexico pricing; JDE Peet's (~37%) grows ~1-2% as green-coffee pass-through pricing fades. EBITDA margin moves from ~24% to 25.2% by year 4 as cost synergies land, net of integration cash costs in years 1-2 and the stranded overhead of two listed companies. The Separation into Beverage Co and Global Coffee Co happens roughly on plan (2027) and is value-neutral: the same flows and the same claims, split across two tickers. Deleveraging is funded by operating cash; no buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Refreshment Beverages keeps compounding high-single digits on energy (GHOST, C4), hydration and Dr Pepper share gains; single-serve stabilises as brewer placements recover (appliance volume +16.7% in Q3-2026, +2.1% in Q2) and K-Cup volume flattens; JDE Peet's holds price as green coffee eases and takes the margin. Synergies exceed plan and EBITDA margin reaches 26.5%. The Separation completes in early 2027 and each company is rated on its own multiple - the terminal cap is 20x rather than 18x. Needs three things to go right at once: beverage momentum, a coffee-category floor, and clean integration.
scenario_narratives.bear: Single-serve is in structural decline, not a destocking cycle: pod volume keeps falling mid-single digits, price has to be given back to retailers and private label, and U.S. Coffee profit (962 in FY2025, down from 1,215 in FY2022) keeps eroding. JDE Peet's turns out to be a low-margin, price-taking European coffee business facing deflation and retailer pushback; CSD volumes soften under sugar taxes and GLP-1 adoption; synergies are consumed by integration overruns and dis-synergies. Margin drifts to 22.5% and growth to 1-1.5%. The Separation slips because leverage does not come down (covenant: 4.0-4.25x pro forma net leverage and investment-grade ratings at both companies), Baa3/BBB- is at risk, and refinancing the $7.3bn of short-term borrowings costs more. With ~$27.7/share of claims ahead of the common, a ~30% lower enterprise value takes more than half of the equity value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: KDP is now a ~$29bn-revenue beverage and coffee group carrying ~$38bn of claims ahead of the common (borrowings, convertible preferred, the Pod JV minority, leases, structured payables, the GHOST put) against ~$7bn of EBITDA. The equity is a levered residual on a slow-growing staple: small changes in enterprise value move the per-share value two to three times as much, which is why the bear and bull cases sit so far apart. The model values the combined entity on unlevered owner free cash flow built from Q2/Q3-2026 run-rate components, deducts every senior claim once, and treats the planned Separation as a re-labelling of the same cash flows rather than a source of value in the base case. SBC is under 1% of revenue, so the house and street values are close and the accounting-regime band is narrow; the financing structure, not SBC, is what matters here.
key_risks_to_valuation: Base revenue and margin rest on two post-acquisition quarters and a pro forma estimate of Q4-2026; purchase accounting is still preliminary and JDE Peet's has no audited history inside KDP.
Leverage: every 1pp of sustainable EBITDA margin is worth roughly $3-4 per share after the ~$27.7/share of senior claims.
Legacy U.S. Coffee: K-Cup pod volume is falling and Q3-2026 profit was flattered by ~$99m of one-off tariff refunds.
Separation timing and terms: contingent on leverage and investment-grade ratings at both companies; the preferred conversion price resets on Separation.
Convertible preferred treated as debt at $4,500m; above $37.25 per share it converts into ~120.8m shares and dilutes instead.
Not in the bridge: any JDE Peet's pension deficit, and the Keurig antitrust litigation (>$1.5bn claimed before partial summary judgment, no accrual).
Green-coffee, aluminium and tariff costs, and EUR translation on ~37% of sales.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E PRO FORMA for a full year of JDE Peet's: 9M-2026 pro forma net sales 21,473 (Q3-2026 10-Q Note 2, line 2754) + Q4-2026E ~7,800 (legacy KDP Q4-2025 4,499 grown ~8% + JDE Peet's ~2,950). Reported FY2026 will be ~26.4bn because Q1 excludes JDE Peet's; that is NOT the run-rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,360.94m common shares issued and outstanding at 2026-09-30 (balance sheet) + 5.3m dilutive stock awards (Q3-2026 EPS note) = 1,366.2m. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 4.5m Series A Convertible Preferred (convertible at $37.25 into ~120.8m common) is NOT in the count; it is carried as a debt-like claim at its $4,500m liquidation preference inside net_debt. Charge once: debt-like XOR as-converted, never both.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30. Cash-flow add-back 'Employee stock-based compensation expense': FY2025 97 - 9M-2025 70 + 9M-2026 95 = 122 (Q3-2026 10-Q line 2449). Plus 'Tax withholdings related to net share settlements' (financing): 31 - 29 + 34 = 36. KDP publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. NOTE: Metrics.csv Q2-2026 (177) and H1-2026 (207) StockBasedComp disagree with the 9M-2026 cash-flow figure of 95 and look mis-extracted; not used.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: reported_fcf is TTM OCF less PP&E purchases: FY2025 1,505 - 9M-2025 (1,279-338) + 9M-2026 (2,220-457) = 2,327. It is a LEVERED figure (after ~$600m+ cash interest), spans one pre-acquisition quarter and carries ~$756m of pre-tax deal/integration/financing costs, so it is not the base the projections compound from; the forward build is unlevered and component-based.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.25% (US 10-year), ERP 5.0%, relevered beta ~0.85 (staple, unlevered ~0.55, ~43% debt-like claims in the capital structure) gives cost of equity ~8.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% at Baa3/BBB- (4.1% after tax). Market-weighted that is ~6.6%; the model uses 7.5% in every scenario as the house floor for a levered staple mid-integration. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights: no per-scenario WACC spread.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP. Operating leases (liability 1,031) are already an operating cost inside EBITDA and are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases use treatment (A): the 988 liability is in net debt, principal payments (146 for 9M-2026, financing) are not deducted from flows, and renewal is charged through capex (finance-lease ROU additions of 172 for 9M-2026, ~0.7% of revenue, are inside capex_pct_path).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI is deducted once in the equity bridge at book 4,205 (2026-09-30). ~3,995 of that is the 49% Pod Manufacturing JV interest sold to Apollo/KKR/Goldman for $4bn in 2026, so book is a fresh transaction price. The JV investor is targeted a 6.375% IRR for five years (~$255m/yr distributions; 64 paid in Q3-2026) and KDP holds a call right in years ~8-15: economically close to a $4bn preferred financing.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon, three scenarios. Chosen because KDP is a branded-beverage and coffee operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; leverage is high but this is not a distressed, financial or property entity, and the pending Separation is a spin-off rather than a cash takeover, so the three-scenario frame holds (no deal-completes/deal-breaks weighting). FIRST VALUATION of this ticker. BASE YEAR: the company changed shape on 2026-04-01 (JDE Peet's acquired, ~$18.4bn); projections compound from pro forma FY2026E revenue of 29.3bn and Q2/Q3-2026 run-rate economics, not from pre-deal KDP. HISTORY: pre-2019 rows belong to Dr Pepper Snapple / Keurig Green Mountain, so CAGRs use FY2019 onward. CAPITAL STRUCTURE: the ~4,418 balance-sheet 'gap' flagged by the parser is the Series A Convertible Perpetual Preferred Stock (mezzanine, 4.75% cash dividend, $4,500m liquidation preference, conversion price $37.25), carried here as debt-like at 4,500. Net debt also includes finance leases, interest-bearing structured payables inherited from JDE Peet's, the 399 owed to untendered JDE Peet's holders (settled 2026-10-26) and the 912 GHOST mandatory redemption liability (flows consolidate 100% of GHOST). The equity bridge deducts NCI and adds equity-method investments and the Chobani note receivable, whose income sits below operating income and is therefore not in the flows. EPS: the Q2-2026 $0.04 and 9M $0.85 are two-class-method figures - net income attributable to KDP (9M 1,294) less the allocation to Preferred Investors (135) over 1,364.9m diluted shares; NCI (138) is deducted before that. Nothing is wrong with the share count. BUYBACKS: none in 2026 (9 in FY2025); the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding, and preferred terms block common buybacks if preferred dividends are deferred. CONVERSION CHECK: preferred holders convert only above $37.25; base and bear values sit at or below that, so debt-like is the right treatment there. In the bull case as-converted treatment would lower the per-share value by roughly 2-3% - not modelled. NOT VERIFIED: JDE Peet's pension deficit (not broken out in the 10-Q) and the Keurig antitrust litigation (remaining plaintiffs claimed >$1.5bn before partial summary judgment; nothing accrued) - neither is in the bridge. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Run-rate: Q3-2026 income from operations 1,333 + integration/restructuring 138 + inventory step-up ~47 + Chobani facility-sale drag ~48 - one-off tariff refunds 99 = ~1,470 (20.0% of sales); plus depreciation ~206 and intangible amortization ~126 per quarter gives EBITDA ~24.5% in a seasonally strong quarter, ~24% for a year. Cross-check: legacy KDP ~30% on 17.9bn plus JDE Peet's ~17.5% on 11.4bn = ~24%. Year 1 is held at 23.6% for cash integration and separation costs (program of $325-400m through Q1-2029); the ramp to 25.2% is the announced cost synergies net of the stranded costs of running two public companies.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: Effective rate 22.6% FY2025, 23.6% 9M-2026; cash taxes 518 vs provision 442 for 9M-2026. Set at 25% rather than ~23% because the engine taxes EBIT after ~$500m/yr of acquired-intangible amortization that is not deductible in a share deal; the extra 2pp removes that phantom shield.
base.capex_rationale: PP&E purchases ~2.9-3.4% of legacy revenue (486-563 in FY2024-25) and ~3% at JDE Peet's, plus finance-lease renewals ~0.7% (treatment A). The 2.3% of Q2/Q3-2026 is integration-year deferral (194 of capex sat unpaid in payables), not a run-rate.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables + inventory (6,290) roughly equal trade payables (6,223); structured payables are counted as debt, so growth is assumed neither to release nor absorb cash.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: leverage has roughly doubled, the rating sits one notch above junk, and integration, a spin-off and a structurally soft single-serve category are being run at the same time - the downside is still margin erosion rather than solvency, so not higher. Base 50%: Q2/Q3-2026 run-rate, reaffirmed FY2026 guidance and announced synergies. Bull cut to 25%: it requires beverage momentum, a floor under single-serve and a clean integration to coincide, and the per-share figure slightly overstates it because the preferred would convert above $37.25.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
